summary: Computed Smith normal forms of the Cartan matrices of star trees T_{x,y,z} for 2≤x≤y≤z≤8 (S≠1): 58 of 81 discriminant groups are cyclic, the rest are not (e.g. T_{2,2,2}=D4 has (Z/2)²). No uniform structure such as cyclic of order xyz(n−4)/n appears, so the lattice route gives no ES constraint.

Verified by Schur complement (and numerically for 12 triple/k combinations): det = xyz(k−3+1/x+1/y+1/z). The central weight k only shifts the numerator, so 'ES with integer offset' is the general numerator-a Egyptian equation, not a new ES lane.
Restatement only: the triangle (π/x,π/y,π/z) has angle sum πS, so its defect is π(1−S) = π(n−4)/n for an ES triple; no tiling or Wythoff content beyond this equation was tested.

Factorised the six known U-failures (105, 2961, 3985, 25305, 111969, 978145): counts of prime factors ≡3 mod 4 with multiplicity are 2, 4, 0, 2, 4, 2. With only six failures the rate test is uninformative; it needs U(n) computed to ≥10^7 to say anything.

Enumerated all solutions x≤y≤z of 4/p=1/x+1/y+1/z for primes p≤1500 (11800 solutions, 237 primes; checked vs brute force for p≤59). The x/p histogram is extremely lopsided: 10027 of 11800 solutions have x/p in [0.25,0.30), only 1 has x/p≥0.55.

From the same enumeration (primes ≤1500, all odd primes, not split by p mod 4): only 1.7% of primes have a solution with z≤10x. The most balanced solution has z/x = 1154 at p=577, so balanced solutions are rare.

Same enumeration, all odd primes ≤1500: min(y−x)=0 first occurs at p=7, and 51% of primes have a solution with y−x≤2. The p≡1 (mod 4) restriction in the item was not split out, so this is a partial answer.

Checked the identity p+1 = 2g + (4C−1)uB for torus knots, where 2g = (u−1)(B−1), against p+u=(4uC−1)B over u,B,C < 30 (0 failures). It is elementary algebra; the Milnor-fibre/Alexander-polynomial reading was not tested.
Restatement: the area of Δ(x,y,z) is π(1−Σ1/x), so a spectrum value equal to (n−4)/n means Σ1/x=4/n, which is ES itself. The step tests nothing beyond the equation.

Already done: BRAINSTORM/bsA_wu_rokhlin_sign.md states the van der Blij/Milgram sign rule for discriminant forms, and the H04 Murasugi-sum signature run (scripts/z52b_p1_H04_tangle_sig.py) shows σ does not determine the (A/p) symbol (both symbols occur at σ=0). ES_CONNECTIONS_TODO.md line ~459 records this.

Hypergeometric exponent differences (1/x,1/y,1/z) with Σ=4/n are triangle groups of area π(n−4)/n. Arithmeticity (Takeuchi's list of arithmetic triangle signatures, cited from memory, not verified) holds for only finitely many signatures, so no ES triple family is arithmetic. No computation was run.
Restatement: planes with integer intercepts through (t,t,t), t=n/4, with normal (1/x,1/y,1/z) are the ES equation rewritten, and no test beyond that equation is proposed.

Took the lattice spanned by the integer vectors (L/x, L/y, L/z) over all solutions for primes p ≤ 400 (L = lcm of each prime's denominators) and computed its Hermite-form index. The index is dominated by the scaling L and varies wildly (e.g. 50, 4080, 84240, …), so the raw index carries no usable invariant; a normalised version (divide by L³ or use the primitive lattice) would be the next step.

Area argument: a d-fold orbifold cover of the ES triangle orbifold multiplies its area by d, so d·(n−4)/n = (n′−4)/n′ gives 4/n′ = 1 − d + 4d/n, which is negative for n > 4d when d ≥ 2. So a naive ES(n)→ES(dn) transport through orbifold covers is impossible; the Jankins–Neumann Seifert Euler-number computation itself was not done.

Test: for a fixed Type II slice, compute the lattice width (min over integer directions of the width of the convex body {(x,y,z) ∈ ℝ³: 1/x+1/y+1/z=4/p, box}) for hard primes and compare with Khinchine's flatness constant. Estimated ~1 h of coding (body construction and width via LP over directions) and a few minutes of compute for p ≤ 10⁴.

summary: Tested the residue set R_p = {x mod p : x a solution coordinate} for primes p ≤ 400 (76 primes): no prime had R_p multiplicatively closed (restricted to |R_p| ≤ 60). No subgroup or coset structure shows up in this first look.

Looked for solutions with arithmetic-progression denominators (y−x = z−y) for all 76 primes ≤ 400: none found. This is a clean negative for the AP sibling in this range; a local obstruction was not checked.
Restatement: n = 4xyz/(xy+yz+zx) is an integer exactly when 4/n = Σ1/x, so enumerating primitive triples and sorting these values only reproduces ES solutions by definition.
Restatement: with y=ku, z=kv, gcd(u,v)=1 the divisibility condition is the scaling of the ES equation, a rewriting with no new test.
Reformulation: a determinant form of the residual factor-pair condition restates the same divisibility; no concrete row-operation test was proposed beyond this rewriting.

Counted, for each a/b in (1,3] with b ≤ 20, the 3-term unit-fraction representations with x≤y≤z. Counts per denominator grow (b=1: 2, b=2: 6, b=8: 21), with no finite-list cut-off in this range. This gives no useful contrast with the spherical classification.

Gauss-reduced L_p = {(x,y): y ≡ i·x mod p} for the 147 primes p ≡ 1 (mod 4) up to 2000. The first minimum is always exactly p (the lattice is the Gaussian-prime lattice of p = a²+b², see Z1705), so the crossing is only in the second basis vector, whose norm changes at every consecutive prime (146 of 146). This is a generic change with no boundary structure found.

The natural polytope for ES is not linear: the constraint 4xyz = n(xy+yz+zx) is quadratic/cubic, so there is no lattice polytope whose Ehrhart family encodes ES. The linear relaxation (box or simplex) carries no ES content.

Same obstruction as Z1103: the forbidden set for an inside-out polytope would have to be the nonlinear ES variety, so no linear family of hyperplanes encodes the exclusion. No ES-specific test is available for this item.

summary: Enumeration confirms the ordering bounds x ∈ (p/4, 3p/4] for all solutions with x≤y≤z (76 primes ≤ 400). Jensen and tangent-line bounds give no sharper constraint on the integer solution set, so no sharper bound was found.

AM–HM gives x+y+z ≥ 9p/4 with equality only at (3p/4)(1,1,1). Over the 76 primes ≤ 400 the integer gap min(x+y+z) − 9p/4 ranges from 5.75 to about 33 306, so integer certificates stay far from the real AM–HM bound.

Lagrange critical point of x+y+z under Σ1/x = 4/p is (3p/4)(1,1,1), which is the AM–HM minimiser. Integer certificates sit 5.75 to ~33 306 above 9p/4 for primes ≤ 400 (Z1169), so the stationary point is not a useful guide to small certificates. No further cost function was tested.

Computed the Hessian of z(x,y) = pxy/(4xy − p(x+y)) symbolically and checked z(a,b) reproduces the third denominator at 8 real solutions (p=409, 1009). The Hessian determinant is positive at all eight points (e.g. 5.5e5 to 4.8e22). The comparison of two sampling schemes was not run.

The scaling x↦λx identifies all nonzero n mod q, so the local motivic count is blind to n.

Riemann–Hurwitz with the ES triangle signature gives an elementary constraint: a surface S with a group G acting with signature (x,y,z), 1/x+1/y+1/z = 4/p, satisfies χ(S) = |G|·(4/p − 1), so 2g−2 = |G|(p−4)/p. Hence p divides |G| for every such G (PROVED from χ, p odd prime). So ES triangle signatures can only be realised by groups whose order is a multiple of p; this is a checkable constraint on any candidate group family (e.g. PSL(2,p)-type groups). The May–Zimmerman construction itself was not read (only abelian-group papers were retrieved).
evidence: web search: Strong symmetric genus spectrum (abelian groups; arXiv 1103.4895)

For all ES solutions with p ≤ 300 (1559 solutions), the weights a=L/x, b=L/y, c=L/z (L=lcm) give (a+b+c)/lcm(a,b,c) = 4L/(p·lcm(a,b,c)). This is never an integer in the sample (e.g. (2,4,20) at p=5 gives 8/5), so the Gorenstein-type integrality fails across the board.
